message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports a quantitative measure of concordance between the animal model's transcriptome and human NASH transcriptomes ('A strong concordance of the mouse gene expression patterns at 8 and 52 weeks to the human NASH transcriptome was observed (FDR 0.02 and 0.08, respectively)').",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "The study describes a model for NASH and HCC, and states 'It is hoped that it will serve as a relevant model to identify therapeutic targets, model disease progression and test preventive and therapeutic approaches against NASH, hepatic fibrosis and HCC.'",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic",
    "oncology",
    "metabolic"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and hepatocellular cancer (HCC), which are hepatic and oncological conditions, and are linked to metabolic syndrome.",
  "model_type": "induced",
  "model_evidence": "The study describes a diet-induced animal model of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and hepatocellular cancer (HCC).",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study describes a diet-induced animal model using mice (C57BL/6J, 129S1/SvImJ, and a B6/129 cross).",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study reports on histological endpoints (steatosis, steatohepatitis, fibrosis, HCC) and transcriptomic endpoints, as well as metabolic parameters (obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia)."
}
